posts.title: structure should follow strategy
posts.description: Jason Zweig has a very interesting observation about Warren Buffet: I like to talk, instead, about structure. In 1962, three years before Buffett took over at Berkshire, the business historian Alfred D. Chandler wrote that “unless structure follows strategy, inefficiency results.” What did he mean? Businesses that design themselves around what they’re trying to achieve are the most likely to succe

posts.title: Start With What You Know
posts.description: Quoting Daniel Stenberg I decided that instead of trying to do this the best and optimal way – I shouldn’t let perfect be the enemy of good – I would start out by doing the things I know how to do and take it as far as I can one step at a time. Something should be better than nothing . Interesting thought process from a great hacker and engineer.
